claims.text: Gas-phase environment governs degradation in additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 through distinct oxidizing and reducing pathways.
High oxygen partial pressure causes rapid formation of continuous intergranular oxide scales.
The oxide scales formed under oxidizing conditions are rich in Cr and Ti.
Oxide formation depletes Cr and Ti from regions adjacent to grain boundaries.
Cr and Ti depletion embrittles grain boundaries and promotes crack initiation.
Under reducing conditions, suppression of surface oxidation permits internal elemental segregation.
Segregation under reducing conditions induces a localized FCC-to-BCC transformation.
BCC regions are more brittle than FCC regions and can reduce ductility.
Brittle BCC regions facilitate stress concentration and premature catastrophic failure under mechanical loading.
The as-built alloy is homogeneous, has a primary FCC matrix, and has minimal preexisting oxide or phase segregation.
Changing only the atmosphere at fixed temperature can distinguish the proposed oxidizing and reducing degradation pathways.
Oxidizing exposure will produce thicker, continuous grain-boundary oxide scales relative to the as-built baseline.
Oxidizing exposure will decrease fracture toughness relative to the as-built baseline.
Reducing exposure will produce minimal surface oxide formation relative to oxidizing exposure.
Reducing exposure will increase localized FCC-to-BCC transformation and compositional segregation relative to the as-built baseline.
Reducing exposure will reduce ductility relative to the as-built baseline.
The proposed behavior applies from 700 to 1000 °C for exposure durations of 24 to 100 hours.
A lack of statistically significant atmosphere-dependent differences in oxide morphology, phase transformation, and mechanical degradation would falsify the proposed mechanistic link.

contradictions.description: The nominal Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni-Ti composition contains no Mn, yet the uncertainty field invokes possible Mn oxidation without identifying Mn as an impurity or added constituent.
